text: Here's the paradox. Men fail in dating because they are not ready to fail. Some guys think that if they get rejected again and again, it means something is wrong with them. That they're not good enough or they just don't have it. They imagine there are guys out there who just say hi to a girl and everything works perfectly. But that's not reality. Rejection isn't proof that you're broken. It's part of the game. In fact, failing and getting turned down is the norm. Success? That's the exception. And yet, it's the exception that makes all the effort worth it. Let's be honest. Dating for the average guy has never been harder. Women have more options than ever. Social media and dating apps change the game. And competition is everywhere. But you still only have two choices. You either give up or you work even harder. That means mistakes, rejections, awkward moments, again and again. But each one teaches you something. You like a girl in your class? Ask her out. You meet a girl at a party? Ask her out. Don't wait for perfect timing. Act. And here's the harsh math. Even if you talk to 100 women, maybe 30% will give you their number. And out of those, if 2 or 3 turn into something bigger, that's already good. But think about it. That also means that 97 women out of 100 rejected you. And that's normal. That's the process. The guys who succeed aren't the ones who never get rejected. They are the ones who get rejected the most, but keep going anyway. So accept rejection as part of life, as part of the process. Fail, learn, repeat. That's how you win. If this hits you, like the video, subscribe, and share it with a friend who needs to hear this today.
